currency.description:
ISO currency code for priced series (`USD`, `EUR`, ...). Index-type codes
return `INDEX` instead: the value is an index level, not a money amount, and
`formatted` carries no currency symbol (`"4340.00"`). Index-type codes are
`BALTIC_DRY_INDEX`, `BALTIC_CAPESIZE_INDEX`, `BALTIC_PANAMAX_INDEX`,
`BALTIC_SUPRAMAX_INDEX` and `SCFI_INDEX`, all with `unit: index`.
This measure and formatting also apply to daily, weekly and monthly
aggregates from the historical and past-window endpoints. The Drewry
World Container Index composite (`CONTAINER_FREIGHT_COMPOSITE_USD`) and its
lanes are priced in dollars per 40ft container and return `USD` with
`unit: usd_per_40ft`.

data_status.description:
Freshness classification of the price, derived from the source session
(`observed_at`) against the series' expected publication cadence
(`freshness.expected_max_age_seconds`), not from the time OilPriceAPI
collected the row.

- `current`: `freshness.age_seconds` is within `expected_max_age_seconds`.
- `delayed`: past the expected cadence but inside the stale limit; the last
  print is still served.
- `stale`: past the stale limit; `stale` is `true`.
- `degraded`: the series' data-gap circuit breaker is open
  (`freshness.circuit_breaker_open: true`) while the value is not yet stale.
- `provisional`: the served print is held from a single source and has not yet
  been confirmed by a second independent source. Reserved for the Baltic
  session-ledger codes (`BALTIC_DRY_INDEX`, `BALTIC_CAPESIZE_INDEX`,
  `BALTIC_PANAMAX_INDEX`, `BALTIC_SUPRAMAX_INDEX`); not served as of 2026-10-10.

Index-type codes print once per London business day (Baltic indices) or once a
week (`SCFI_INDEX` on Friday, `CONTAINER_FREIGHT_COMPOSITE_USD` on Thursday),
so `delayed` between prints is the normal state for them, not an error. To tell
"old because weekly" from "old because broken", compare `freshness.age_seconds`
with `freshness.expected_max_age_seconds`.

Live example (2026-10-10, `/v1/prices/latest?by_code=BALTIC_CAPESIZE_INDEX`):
`price: 4340.0`, `formatted: "4340.00"`, `currency: "INDEX"`, `unit: "index"`,
`observed_at: "2026-10-09T12:00:00.000Z"`, `data_status: "current"`,
`freshness: {status: "current", age_seconds: 81475, expected_max_age_seconds: 324000}`.

info.description:
Source-aware oil and energy data API. Check each endpoint's source timestamp,
coverage, and freshness fields before using a response in a time-sensitive workflow.

## Authentication

API-key endpoints use `Authorization: Token YOUR_API_KEY`. Operations that do
not require an API key explicitly declare an empty security requirement.
`/v1/demo/prices` is keyless.

## Rate Limiting

- Free tier: 50 requests per day
- Paid tiers have plan-specific monthly quotas.
- `402` means the allowance is exhausted: a Free or post-trial caller
  must upgrade, and a paid plan has used its monthly allowance (the body
  carries `MONTHLY_QUOTA_EXCEEDED` and reset metadata, so do not retry before
  the reset). `429` means an active-trial allowance or a rolling rate limit
  (for example the hourly safety limit) is exceeded; retry `429` and transient
  `5xx` responses with bounded backoff.
- Website login and signup (`POST /sessions` and `POST /users`) also enforce
  authentication-attempt limits independently of API plan quotas: 3 attempts
  per normalized email address in 5 minutes, and 3 attempts per minute per
  verified visitor IP. Requests without a verified proxy identity retain
  the existing 20 requests/minute IP ceiling. A `429` on these routes means
  wait for `Retry-After` before retrying; upgrading a plan does not remove
  authentication-attempt limits.

Futures curves are never refused because a market is closed or a session has
just reopened. The last available data is served with `metadata.freshness_status`,
`metadata.stale`, `metadata.latest_data_at` and `metadata.stale_by_minutes`:
`outside_market_hours` while the venue is closed (weekend, daily break,
holiday); `awaiting_first_print` for the first 30 minutes of a new session
while only a valid prior close exists; `degraded` when the market is open and
the source is behind. None of these is a fresh trade; source timestamps remain
unchanged. Data older than the 96-hour serving bound is refused with 503.

Gasoil reports `metadata.freshness_status: no_recent_trades` when the
benchmark contract has not traded within 30 minutes but our collector confirmed
the quote within that window and the curve printed within 90 minutes. The last
trade is served with its true `latest_data_at` and `stale_by_minutes`, plus
`source_checked_at` and `curve_latest_trade_at`.

Paid monthly-cap responses include `retry_guidance`: immediate retries cannot
restore quota. When a representative sample supports it, `batching_opportunity`
describes an estimated lower request rate; batching does not restore an already
exhausted allowance. It may replace an unnecessary upgrade recommendation.

## Continuous futures coverage

On `/v1/futures/continuous/brent`, `/v1/futures/continuous/wti` and their
`/historical` routes, `metadata.history_available_from` is the earliest
stored public continuous futures source date, falling back to collection
date for older imports without a source timestamp. It is a date string or
null when no public observations exist. Coverage metadata is cached for up
to one hour and does not promise observations or volume on every later date.
It describes the archive independently of the request's date range; account
depth limits remain in `metadata.history_window` on historical responses.
Latest-response `metadata.total_historical_records` counts stored public
snapshots, including revisions, rather than distinct source dates. Latest
quotes and their prior-day comparisons exclude private organization rows
and other price types. Repeated source timestamps select the later collected
revision; the oldest metadata/response cache formats are no longer used.

## Spread and indicator query parameters

Spread and indicator endpoints reject unrecognized query parameter names with
HTTP 400 and `error.code: UNKNOWN_PARAMETERS`, after authentication and access
checks. The error includes `unrecognized_parameters`, `allowed_parameters`,
and a `suggestions` map for recognized date-name mistakes; values are not
echoed. Use the parameters documented for the specific operation. Historical
endpoints accept `start_date` and `end_date`, not `from`, `to`, or `period`.
For WTI crack history use `crude=WTI_USD&type=3-2-1&start_date=2013-01-01`,
not `code=WTI_321_CRACK&from=2013-01-01`. Latest endpoints do not accept
history-only dates. Existing `api_key`, `token`, and `format` transport
parameters remain supported. Retired endpoints retain their 410 response.

## Account and onboarding metadata

Email signup (`POST /users`, under `user`) and Google signup (`POST /oauth/google`,
at the top level) accept optional `signup_use_case`: `fuel_app`, `trading_quant`,
`logistics`, `bi_dashboard`, or `other`. Unknown or non-string values are ignored.
The first signup value is immutable; subsequent sign-ins do not overwrite it.
Account responses expose the stored value, or null for an older/skipped signup.

Both signup routes also accept an optional first-touch `msclkid` string
(nested under `user` for email signup, top-level for Google signup). It is
stored for attribution only when the account is created; repeat sign-ins
and account linking do not replace it. Account responses do not expose it.

Both signup routes accept optional `signup_referrer_path` with the same
nesting as `msclkid`. It records the public page immediately before signup
as a pathname only, such as `/quick-start`. Paths with queries, private
account/auth/checkout prefixes, invalid characters, or more than 255 characters are
discarded without failing signup. Only account creation writes the value;
older accounts remain null and account responses do not expose it.

`POST /auth/magic_link` returns identical guidance for existing and unknown
addresses, with `retry_after_seconds: 60`. A successful response acknowledges
the request, not delivery. A request during the one-minute send cooldown may
reuse the existing email; links and codes expire after 15 minutes.

Successful authenticated JSON object responses include `meta.account_notice`
while an unconfirmed account is subject to the confirmation cap. Its content
matches the confirmation headers and dashboard user notice. CSV and error
responses retain their existing contracts.

`GET /v1/dashboard` adds `billing.contract`: `enforced_limit` and
`effective_capacity` (request counts), `limit_source` (enforcement policy),
`usage_window`, `internal_service`, `support` (display strings), and `addons`
(`futures`, `drilling`, `websocket` booleans). Enabled data access may come from
a plan, trial, or add-on; it does not assert that an add-on was purchased.
Older cached dashboard responses may omit this additive object.

Use `GET /v1/commodities` for the current catalog. Endpoint-level metadata
is authoritative for authentication, plan access, source, and freshness.

get.description:
Calendar-month average of the EIA U.S. on-highway diesel price (series
`EMD_EPD2D_PTE_NUS_DPG`, "Diesel (On-Highway) - All Types", USD per
gallon), the index monthly rail fuel-surcharge programs are keyed to.

Each month carries two separate figures. `eia_monthly_average` is the
value EIA publishes for the month, served as published (`kind:
published`). `weekly_mean` is OilPriceAPI's arithmetic mean of EIA's
weekly prints dated in the month, rounded half up to 3 decimals (`kind:
calculated`), with the weeks used and the week count. For the open
month `eia_monthly_average` is null, `weekly_mean` is the month-to-date
mean and `provisional` is true. When a weekly print EIA has already
published is not held, `weekly_mean.value` is null and `warning` says
why; nothing is interpolated.

`effective_month` is the basis month plus two calendar months. That
convention is listed in `surcharge_lag.verified_programs` only for the
programs whose public page states it; `surcharge_lag.exceptions` lists
a program that uses a different basis period. The applicable tariff or
contract governs.

With no parameters the response holds the current month and the two
before it, newest first. Available on every plan. EIA revises its
values; a revised value is served with `revised_at` and
`previous_value`. EIA's API carries no release timestamp, so
`first_seen_at` is when OilPriceAPI first read the value.

parameters.description: One calendar month as `YYYY-MM`. Cannot be combined with `start_month` or `end_month`.
parameters.name: month

parameters.description: First month of a range as `YYYY-MM`. At most 120 months per request.
parameters.name: start_month

parameters.description: Last month of a range as `YYYY-MM`. Defaults to the current month.
parameters.name: end_month

weekly_mean.method: Arithmetic mean of the EIA weekly prints dated in the month, rounded half up to 3 decimals.

series.name: U.S. No 2 Diesel Retail Prices: Diesel (On-Highway) - All Types
series.release_date_note: EIA API v2 carries no release timestamp. first_seen_at is when OilPriceAPI first read the value from EIA, not EIA's release date.

surcharge_lag.description: effective_month is the second calendar month after basis_month. It applies to the programs listed in verified_programs only.

exceptions.basis: Half-month application periods, each based on an OHD average over a stated two-week basis period, not a calendar month.

surcharge_lag.notice: Not affiliated with or endorsed by any railroad. Planning reference only; the applicable tariff or contract governs.

verified_programs.program: Carload rate-based standard HDF fuel surcharge
verified_programs.statement: The surcharge will be billed to applicable shipments beginning the second month following the month on which the DOE average price calculation was based.

The fuel surcharge is applied to each shipment having a bill of lading dated on or after the 1st day of the second calendar month following the calendar month of a given OHD Average Price calculation.
The fuel surcharge is calculated monthly based on the average On-Highway Diesel Fuel (OHD) of two months prior (e.g. February surcharge is based upon December's average OHD price).

last_successful_refresh_at.description: When both the weekly and monthly series were last read from EIA successfully.

stale.description: True when EIA has not been read successfully in the last 36 hours. Stored values are still served.

series.description: The EIA series, its units and EIA's own pages for it.

surcharge_lag.description: The basis-month-plus-2 rule, the programs it was verified for with their sources, and known exceptions.

The code is in `data.code`.

404.description: A month before the first month held (`MONTH_BEFORE_COVERAGE`, with `data.coverage`) or no data yet (`NO_DATA`).
